description: Empirical reasoning schemas and archetypes for terminal navigation, shell execution, project structure, npm, and Git workflows.

archetypes.name: Working-Directory-Safe CLI Path Resolver
archetypes.coreConcept: Resolving user-supplied relative paths against an explicit current working directory (cwd) using path normalization rather than string concatenation or script-directory assumptions, and enforcing workspace root containment when required.
mentalModel: 1. Distinguish the caller's current working directory (cwd) from the script's own install directory (__dirname / import.meta.dirname).
2. Resolve relative targets against the explicit cwd using path.resolve(cwd, target) instead of manual string concatenation.
3. Verify root containment via path.relative(root, resolved) when a CLI must not escape the project directory.
archetypes.governingInvariant: resolvedTarget = path.resolve(explicitCwd, relativeArg) with explicit root-containment check when scoped

cognitiveTraps.name: Manual String Concatenation for Paths
cognitiveTraps.description: Joining paths with `cwd + '/' + target` fails on trailing slashes, `.` or `..` segments, and non-POSIX separators.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass cwd='/app/' and target='../secret.txt'; string concatenation yields '/app//../secret.txt' without normalizing.

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Script Directory with Working Directory
cognitiveTraps.description: Resolving user-provided relative paths against `__dirname` / `import.meta.dirname` instead of `cwd` looks inside the CLI's install folder rather than the user's project.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Invoke `node /opt/cli/scan.js ./src` from `/workspace/app`; resolving against `__dirname` looks in `/opt/cli/src` instead of `/workspace/app/src`.

cognitiveTraps.name: Unbounded Parent Directory Traversal
cognitiveTraps.description: Accepting `../` segments without checking `path.relative(root, resolved)` allows a CLI to read or write outside the intended workspace root.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass target='../../outside.txt' to a workspace-scoped resolver without checking whether the resolved path starts outside root.

realWorldDomains.description: Resolving target directories and config files passed to a Node CLI from any working directory.
Mapping relative source and output paths inside a project workspace.

qualityChecks.check: Path-resolution helpers accept an explicit `cwd` or `rootDir` parameter rather than reading `process.cwd()` inside core logic.
qualityChecks.why: Reading `process.cwd()` deep inside helpers couples pure path logic to global process state and makes unit tests brittle.

qualityChecks.check: Path manipulation uses normalized path primitives (`path.resolve`, `path.join`, `path.relative`) rather than manual `/` or `\\` string concatenation or splitting.
qualityChecks.why: Manual separator string math breaks on trailing slashes, dot segments, and cross-platform separators.

archetypes.name: CLI Argument, Environment & Exit Code Contract
archetypes.coreConcept: Parsing CLI arguments (argv) and environment variables (env) with explicit precedence (CLI flag > env var > default), separating stdout data from stderr diagnostics, and returning deterministic exit codes without terminating the process inside testable modules.
mentalModel: 1. Design the core CLI runner as a function taking `(argv, env)` and returning `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`.
2. Apply precedence: CLI flag overrides environment variable, which overrides default; check `!== undefined` rather than truthiness.
3. Reserve `exitCode = 0` for success and non-zero (e.g. `1` or `2`) for errors, keeping `process.exit()` only in the thin bin wrapper.
archetypes.governingInvariant: exitCode === 0 iff execution succeeded; stdout contains output data, stderr contains diagnostics; core runner never calls process.exit()

cognitiveTraps.name: Calling process.exit() Inside Testable Logic
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling `process.exit(1)` inside a helper or runner function kills the test runner process instead of returning a testable exit status.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call `runCli(['--invalid'], {})` inside `node --test`; `process.exit(1)` aborts the entire test suite.

cognitiveTraps.name: Writing Error Diagnostics to stdout
cognitiveTraps.description: Printing error messages to `stdout` instead of `stderr` breaks downstream shell pipelines and JSON consumers.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Run `node cli.js --missing > out.json`; `out.json` receives the error string instead of remaining empty.

cognitiveTraps.name: Returning Exit Code 0 After Handling an Error
cognitiveTraps.description: Catching an error, logging a message, and exiting with `0` causes `cmd1 && cmd2` in the shell to proceed after failure.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Run `node validate.js missing.json && echo OK`; if exitCode is 0, the shell prints OK despite validation failure.

realWorldDomains.description: Building a configurable CLI command that reads flags, env vars, and reports status via exit codes.
Running a preflight check script that gates shell pipelines with exit codes 0 vs 1.

qualityChecks.check: Core CLI runner and argument-parsing functions return an exit code or throw rather than calling `process.exit()` directly; `process.exit()` is restricted to the top-level bin wrapper.
qualityChecks.why: Calling `process.exit()` inside core modules terminates test runners and prevents callers from composing the CLI logic.

qualityChecks.check: CLI runner and config helpers read arguments and environment variables from injected parameters (`argv`, `env`) rather than hardcoding global `process.argv` and `process.env` inside core logic.
qualityChecks.why: Hardcoding global `process.argv` and `process.env` inside helpers prevents deterministic, parallel-safe unit testing.

archetypes.name: JS Project Layout, Manifest & Ignore Rules
archetypes.coreConcept: Organizing and validating standard JavaScript project layouts (`package.json`, `src/`, `tests/`, `node_modules/`, `.gitignore`) so entrypoints resolve relative to the package root and generated or secret files stay untracked.
mentalModel: 1. Anchor all project paths (`main`, `bin`, `src/`, `tests/`, `.gitignore`) to the directory containing `package.json`.
2. Verify that `node_modules/` and `.env` are excluded in `.gitignore` while `package.json`, `src/`, and `tests/` remain tracked.
3. Inspect filesystem state non-destructively before creating or repairing missing layout entries.
archetypes.governingInvariant: All package.json entrypoints resolve inside projectRoot, and node_modules/ + .env are covered by .gitignore without touching authored src/ or tests/

cognitiveTraps.name: Omitting node_modules or .env from .gitignore
cognitiveTraps.description: Leaving `node_modules/` or `.env` out of `.gitignore` exposes secrets and bloats commits with installed dependencies.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Inspect `.gitignore` in a scaffolded project; `node_modules/` is absent, causing `git status` to track installed packages.

cognitiveTraps.name: Absolute or OS-Specific Paths in package.json
cognitiveTraps.description: Writing machine-specific absolute paths (e.g. `/home/dev/app/src/index.js`) in `package.json` breaks the project on every other machine.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Set `main` to `/home/alice/project/src/index.js`; `require('.')` fails on CI with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

cognitiveTraps.name: Assuming CWD Is Always the Project Root
cognitiveTraps.description: Checking for `package.json` or `src/` using bare relative paths fails whenever a script is invoked from a subdirectory.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Run a layout check from `project/src/`; bare `fs.existsSync('package.json')` returns false.

realWorldDomains.description: Auditing a Node project directory for valid package.json, src/, tests/, and .gitignore rules.
Safely creating missing project folders and baseline files without clobbering existing code.

qualityChecks.check: Filesystem scaffolding or repair helpers check for existing files/directories first and never overwrite or delete existing authored files (`src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`).
qualityChecks.why: Unconditional writes or recursive deletes can silently destroy existing learner or production source code.

qualityChecks.check: Project layout validators anchor all file lookups to an explicit `projectRoot` parameter rather than assuming the caller's `cwd` is the project root.
qualityChecks.why: Invoking a tool from a nested subdirectory causes bare relative lookups like `'package.json'` to miss the real project root.
